items.q: A 48-year-old man with chronic severe alcohol dependence is brought to the emergency department with confusion, horizontal nystagmus, and truncal ataxia. Administration of intravenous glucose without prior thiamine administration risks precipitating acute lactic acidosis and neurological worsening due to impairment of which enzyme complex?
items.exp: The pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase require thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP, vitamin B1) as an essential cofactor. In thiamine deficiency, glucose loading drives glycolysis but pyruvate cannot enter the TCA cycle via PDH, accumulating and converting into lactic acid, which precipitates severe lactic acidosis and Wernicke encephalopathy.
r: Incorrect. PFK-1 does not require thiamine pyrophosphate.
Correct. Pyruvate dehydrogenase requires thiamine pyrophosphate; glucose without thiamine worsens Wernicke encephalopathy.
Incorrect. Citrate synthase does not require thiamine.
Incorrect. Lactate dehydrogenase uses NADH, not thiamine.
items.kp: Pyruvate dehydrogenase requires thiamine pyrophosphate; administering glucose without thiamine precipitates acute Wernicke encephalopathy.

items.q: Which enzyme of the citric acid cycle is directly embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane and functions as Complex II of the electron transport chain?
items.exp: Succinate dehydrogenase is the only citric acid cycle enzyme bound to the inner mitochondrial membrane, directly reducing FAD to FADH2 and feeding electrons into the ubiquinone pool as Complex II.
r: Correct. Succinate dehydrogenase is embedded in the inner membrane and serves as Complex II of the ETC.
Incorrect. Citrate synthase is a soluble matrix enzyme.
Incorrect. Isocitrate dehydrogenase is a soluble matrix enzyme.
Incorrect. Fumarase is a soluble matrix enzyme.

items.q: A patient with lactic acidosis is found to have an allosteric enzyme deficiency. Which step in glycolysis is considered the primary, committed rate-limiting step regulated by ATP, AMP, and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate?
items.exp: Phosphofructokinase-1 catalyzes the irreversible phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate. It is allosterically stimulated by AMP and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate and inhibited by ATP and citrate.
r: Correct. PFK-1 is the primary committed rate-limiting step of glycolysis.
Incorrect. Hexokinase is an early regulated step but not the committed step because G6P enters glycogen synthesis and the HMP shunt.
Incorrect. Pyruvate kinase is regulated but acts at the end of the pathway.
Incorrect. GAPDH is a reversible enzyme.

items.q: Arsenate poisoning exerts toxicity during glycolysis by competing with inorganic phosphate at which specific enzymatic step, resulting in zero net ATP generation?
items.exp: Arsenate competes with inorganic phosphate as a substrate for GAPDH, forming unstable 1-arseno-3-phosphoglycerate which spontaneously hydrolyzes, bypassing substrate-level phosphorylation and preventing net ATP generation.
r: Correct. Arsenate uncouples GAPDH by substituting for inorganic phosphate.
Incorrect. Phosphoglycerate kinase produces ATP from 1,3-BPG, which is bypassed by arsenolysis.
Incorrect. Pyruvate kinase generates ATP downstream.
Incorrect. Enolase is inhibited by fluoride.

items.q: Fluoride is added to blood collection tubes used for plasma glucose estimation because it potently inhibits which glycolytic enzyme by complexing with magnesium?
items.exp: Fluoride ions form a complex with magnesium and phosphate that binds and inhibits enolase, stopping glycolysis in red cells and preventing in vitro artifactual decline of measured blood glucose.
r: Correct. Fluoride inhibits enolase, preserving plasma glucose in blood collection vials.
Incorrect. Pyruvate kinase is downstream and not directly inhibited by fluoride.
Incorrect. Phosphoglucose isomerase is an earlier reversible step.
Incorrect. Aldolase cleaves F-1,6-BP into trioses.

items.q: How many total molecules of NADH, FADH2, and GTP/ATP are generated directly per single turn of the citric acid cycle from one molecule of acetyl-CoA?
items.exp: Each turn of the citric acid cycle oxidizing one acetyl-CoA generates 3 NADH (via isocitrate, alpha-ketoglutarate, and malate dehydrogenases), 1 FADH2 (via succinate dehydrogenase), and 1 GTP (via succinyl-CoA synthetase).
r: Correct. One cycle yields 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, and 1 GTP.
Incorrect. FADH2 is produced only at succinate dehydrogenase (1 molecule).
Incorrect. Only 3 NADH are generated in the cycle itself.
Incorrect. Succinyl-CoA synthetase yields 1 high-energy phosphate.

items.q: A researcher observes that addition of malonate halts respiration in isolated liver mitochondria. Malonate acts as a competitive inhibitor of which enzyme?
items.exp: Malonate has a chemical structure (dicarboxylic acid with 3 carbons) highly homologous to succinate (4 carbons), making it a classic competitive inhibitor of succinate dehydrogenase.
r: Correct. Malonate structurally mimics succinate, competitively inhibiting succinate dehydrogenase.
Incorrect. Malate dehydrogenase oxidizes malate to oxaloacetate.
Incorrect. Citrate synthase condenses acetyl-CoA with oxaloacetate.
Incorrect. Alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase is inhibited by succinyl-CoA and NADH.

items.q: Which enzyme of the citric acid cycle catalyzes a substrate-level phosphorylation reaction that produces GTP in the liver and kidneys?
items.exp: Succinyl-CoA synthetase cleaves the high-energy thioester bond of succinyl-CoA, coupling this exergonic cleavage to the phosphorylation of GDP to GTP (or ADP to ATP in muscle).
r: Correct. Succinyl-CoA synthetase catalyzes substrate-level phosphorylation forming GTP.
Incorrect. Succinate dehydrogenase generates FADH2.
Incorrect. Alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase generates NADH and succinyl-CoA.
Incorrect. Isocitrate dehydrogenase generates NADH and CO2.

items.q: Under anaerobic conditions in exercising skeletal muscle, pyruvate is converted to lactate by lactate dehydrogenase. What is the essential physiological purpose of this reaction?
o: Regeneration of NAD+ to sustain continued glycolytic flux at GAPDH
Generation of additional high-energy ATP molecules
Buffering intracellular pH to prevent acidosis
items.exp: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) requires NAD+ to maintain glycolysis. Under anaerobic conditions, mitochondrial reoxidation of NADH is impaired; lactate dehydrogenase reduces pyruvate to lactate while reoxidizing NADH to NAD+.
r: Correct. Lactate dehydrogenase regenerates NAD+ required for GAPDH, allowing continued anaerobic ATP production.
Incorrect. The conversion of pyruvate to lactate produces no ATP directly.
Incorrect. Lactic acid accumulation lowers pH.
Incorrect. Pyruvate dehydrogenase is inactive under hypoxia.
items.kp: Anaerobic conversion of pyruvate to lactate by LDH regenerates cytosolic NAD+, sustaining continued glycolysis at the GAPDH step.

items.q: A child with persistent hyperlactatemia is diagnosed with pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficiency. Which amino acid should be enriched in the diet because its catabolism yields only acetyl-CoA without producing pyruvate?
items.exp: Leucine and lysine are exclusively ketogenic amino acids; their degradation yields acetyl-CoA and acetoacetate without ever forming pyruvate or intermediate gluconeogenic precursors, avoiding lactic acid accumulation.
r: Correct. Leucine is exclusively ketogenic, bypassing pyruvate formation entirely.
Incorrect. Alanine transaminates directly to pyruvate, worsening lactic acidosis.
Incorrect. Glutamine is glucogenic, entering the TCA cycle via alpha-ketoglutarate.
Incorrect. Glycine enters gluconeogenesis via serine and pyruvate.
